picks.editorial_note: An international team led by TU Wien physicist Mario Krenn published in Nature showing AI can autonomously propose novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups — a landmark demonstration of AI accelerating fundamental scientific discovery.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: EPFL researchers built a framework that trains LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty when proposing experiments, a foundational advance for making AI-guided scientific discovery more trustworthy and efficient across disciplines.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: USF, Purdue, and UT Dallas won a $1.2M NSF grant to build quantum-resistant, AI-enabled security for next-generation wireless networks, a tri-institution collaboration tackling a critical national security and infrastructure need.
picks.title: USF faculty secure $1.2M NSF grant to advance quantum-secure, AI-enabled wireless networks

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen spinoff Black Semiconductor won a major engineering award for graphene-based chips that move data optically instead of electrically, a breakthrough with real implications for the energy efficiency of future AI hardware.
picks.title: Light Instead of Electricity: Aachen Engineering Award for a Technological Breakthrough | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Washington University in St. Louis researchers secured NSF funding to build a hybrid neuromorphic-quantum computing system that exploits thermal noise, a novel approach that could dramatically cut the energy cost of AI computing.
picks.title: Grant funds hybrid system that could spur vast energy improvements to computing

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's autonomous research vehicle 'karl.' received a nationwide German testing permit — a rare regulatory milestone signaling growing government confidence in open-source autonomous vehicle platforms.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Helmholtz researchers made a high-profile policy argument that Germany and Europe must build sovereign open frontier AI models rather than depend on US and Chinese systems, sharpening a consequential debate over AI infrastructure independence.
picks.title: Why we in Germany and Europe need to build our own open frontier models

picks.editorial_note: Federal agency AHRQ's cancellation of a Johns Hopkins AI-driven diagnostic research grant shows how funding cuts are directly curtailing promising healthcare AI research, a policy shift with real consequences for patient care.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient

picks.editorial_note: Three Aalto University researchers won competitive ERC Starting Grants, including funding for new mathematical foundations of safe reinforcement learning — a signal of Europe's continued investment in foundational AI research talent.
picks.title: Three rising Aalto University researchers secure highly sought-after EU funding | Aalto University

picks.editorial_note: UAB startup Spiromatics is commercializing AI-driven biomarkers from lung imaging to improve diagnosis of diseases like COPD, translating years of university research into real-world clinical impact.
picks.title: UAB startup brings decades of research to the future of lung care
